neighbours.label: A costumed action-hero role word (superheroes, crime fighter, spy, secret agent) in children's fiction or cartoons, vs the same sentences with an everyday role
fire: For his birthday party, Leo wanted every guest to come dressed as superheroes.
The new cartoon is about a talking dog who becomes a crime fighter at night.
In the picture book, a shy girl turns out to be a secret spy for the queen.
My nephew drew a comic where his cat and hamster are superheroes with capes.
The animated series follows a teenage crime fighter and her robot sidekick.
On Saturday mornings we watched a show about a clumsy spy who always saved the day.
The toy store had a whole wall of action figures of masked superheroes.
In the bedtime story, a little turtle dreams of being a caped crime fighter.
quiet: For his birthday party, Leo wanted every guest to come dressed in pajamas.
The new cartoon is about a talking dog who becomes a mail carrier in town.
In the picture book, a shy girl turns out to be a gifted painter for the queen.
My nephew drew a comic where his cat and hamster are neighbours with gardens.
The animated series follows a teenage gardener and her robot sidekick.
On Saturday mornings we watched a show about a clumsy chef who always burned dinner.
The toy store had a whole wall of stuffed animals and wooden trains.
In the bedtime story, a little turtle dreams of being a fast runner.

predictions: Fire items 0.4-1.0 on the hero-role word; near misses under 0.25. Proper names like Batman are weaker.
